proposals.before_proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
A full-support relation selects at least two true
values in every window, since selections are even
and nonzero. Consequently the moderate certificates
and the saturation graph of
Section~\ref{p14:cert:section} apply to these families,
without any primitivity assumption.

Use the parameters in
\eqref{p1:core:primitive-parameters}.
The total independent weight of moderate
certificates is \(N^{-2\beta+4/A_0+o(1)}
=N^{-91/50+o(1)}\), by
Lemma~\ref{p1:core:moderate}.
If a family has no moderate certificate, every
unmarked vertex has a neighbour in the saturation
graph. The tilted generating function of
Lemma~\ref{p1:core:generator}, now with no factor
for rank loss, bounds its weight beyond size \(s_0\)
by \(O_u(N^{-s_0\delta/2})\).
Choose a fixed \(s_0>\max(s,5000)\).
Both large-size contributions are smaller than
\(N^{-1+\varepsilon}\).

For each of the finitely many \(s\le r<s_0\),
Proposition~\ref{p1:arith:fixed-support} gives
\[
 |\mathcal H_{r,N}|
       \ll_{r,C,\varepsilon}
             N^{r-2r/(2r+1)+\varepsilon}.
 \]
Multiplying by \((up)^r/r!\), and using
\(2r/(2r+1)\ge2s/(2s+1)\), completes the proof.
The factor \(1/r!\) counts unordered sets; it is
not a bound for the growth of an arithmetic
constant in \(r\).
\end{proof}
proposals.proposed_proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Apply Lemma~\ref{p13:transfer:independent-tail} with \(v=u\) and \(a=1\),
and increase its fixed cutoff to \(s_0\ge s\) if necessary.
On \(G\) the exact marginals equal \(p\). Each set of \(r\) distinct
starts has exactly \(r!\) orderings, so the factor \(1/r!\) cancels
exactly. The contribution with \(r\ge s_0\) is therefore bounded by
the unordered tail of that lemma, \(O(N^{-1+\eta})\).
For the finitely many \(s\le r<s_0\), apply
Proposition~\ref{p1:arith:fixed-support} with all \(r\) projections nonzero.
It gives \(|\mathcal H_{r,N}|\ll N^{r/2+\eta}\), hence a weighted
contribution \(O_{r,u,C,\eta}(N^{-r/2+\eta})\).
Since \(r/2\ge1>2s/(2s+1)\), choosing \(\eta>0\) inside the requested
margin and summing these finitely many layers proves the result.
\end{proof}

proposals.title: T22.1 : réutiliser la queue indépendante et le compte fixe renforcé
proposals.finding: La preuve refait les certificats modérés et le générateur des grandes tailles, puis utilise encore la puissance plus faible de T1.14. Le lemme15.8, avec cutoff fixé avant la marge, et T1.14 dans sa version renforcée fournissent une preuve courte de l’énoncé inchangé.
objects_and_quantifiers: s≥2, u>0 et C sont fixés avant N. Choisir a=1, v=u, D=1, Q=2 dans uniform_tail; prendre s0=max(s,s_tail), avec sa monotonie positive. s0 précède le choix final η.

IndependentFullSupportTail.FullSupport exige une unique relation de somme nulle à projections toutes non nulles dans les espaces effectifs S_x. Il ne faut pas le remplacer par une condition de primitivité.

La queue est initialement pondérée par les vraies marginales p_x. Sa restriction aux fenêtres régulières G donne exactement p_x=p. Les familles de la proposition sont une sous-famille positive de la queue du dyadicBlock entier.
Chaque ensemble de r centres distincts a r! énumérations; la division par r! est donc exacte. Aucun majorant d’une constante fixe en fonction d’un ordre croissant n’est utilisé.

Seuls les s≤r<s0, donc un nombre fini d’ordres fixés avant N, utilisent critical_interval_count à s=r. Le compte est N^(r/2+η), le poids est O_{r,u,C}(N^-r), et r/2≥1>2s/(2s+1). Une marge η<ε/2 et le maximum fini des seuils suffisent.

proposals.before_proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Write \(x=at-i_0\), \(y=bt-j_0\), choosing the lower orientation.
As in Lemma~\ref{p1:arith:palmrank}, the normalized old values lie in
a fixed-width interval about \(abt\).  An aligned target has the form
\(z=(ct+h)/d\), with \((c,d)=1\), numerator, denominator and offsets
of polynomial size in \(B\).
The dyadic positions require
\(b/2\leq c/d\leq2a\), up to \(B^{O(1)}/N\).
Separation of rational fractions excludes strict violations of this
interval once \(N\) is large.
Either equality forces \(at=N+B^{O(1)}\) or \(bt=2N+B^{O(1)}\);
these give the stated exceptional sources.

For the interior fractions, a new offset \(k\) matched to a true old
value satisfies one of
\[
 h+dk\equiv0\pmod{c/(c,a)},\qquad
 h+dk\equiv0\pmod{c/(c,b)}.
\]
Their intersection has modulus \(c\).
The union contains at most
\[
 B\,\frac{(c,a)+(c,b)-1}{c}+O(1)
\]
new positions.  The same residual argument as in
Lemma~\ref{p1:arith:palmrank} leaves only \(o(L)\) further dimensions.
Matching to a value in an enclosing interval but absent from the true
old set contributes no new freedom.

Suppose \(c\nmid a\) and \(c\nmid b\), and put \(g=(c,a)\), \(h_1=(c,b)\).
These numbers are coprime and \(gh_1\mid c\).
If one equals one, the other is a proper divisor of \(c\), giving
density at most \(1/2\).
Otherwise \(g,h_1\geq2\) and
\[
 \frac{g+h_1-1}{c}
 \leq\frac1g+\frac1{h_1}-\frac1{gh_1}\leq\frac23.
\]
The last maximum occurs at the smallest coprime pair \(\{2,3\}\).
When \(c>b(a+b-1)\), the density is less than \(1/b\).
All other nonphysical fractions are included in
\eqref{p1:arith:gamma-fixed-channel}.

If \(c\mid a\), a proper divisor has \(c\leq a/2<b/2\), which is
impossible here; thus \(c=a,d=1\).
Similarly \(c\mid b\) leaves only \(c=b,d=1\).
These are the physical fractions reproducing one old family.
Compatibility gives distance at least \(L\) from that source, so the
two true windows share at most one value.
Matches to the other old family have steps \(a,b\) in intervals of
width \(B\), and number at most \(B/b+O(1)\).
This proves the rank bound in these cases as well.

retained_statement.tex:
\begin{lemma}[Additional rank in a fixed channel]
\label{p1:arith:fixed-channel-rank}
One has \(\gamma_{a:b}\leq2/3\).
Apart from \(B^{O_{a,b}(1)}\) source pairs at the dyadic endpoints,
every aligned target \(z\ne x,y\) compatible with a source
\((x,y)\in\mathcal G_{a:b}\) satisfies
\[
 \delta_{x,y}(z):=
 L-\dim\frac{S_x+S_y+S_z}{S_x+S_y}
 \leq\gamma_{a:b}L+o_{a,b,C}(L).
\]
This definition includes any internal rank deficiency of the new window.
The bound remains true when the prime signs of \(a,b\) are included in
the old information.
\end{lemma}

proposals.before_proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Expanding the first four factorial moments with the individual $p_i$
gives the exact identity
\begin{align}
 \kappa_4={}&24\sum_{|I|=4}c(I)-12(C_2^{\mathrm s})^2
 -24\sum_{|T|=3}\Bigl(\sum_{i\in T}p_i\Bigr)c(T)\notag\\
 &+24\sum_{e=\{i,j\}}(p_i^2+p_ip_j+p_j^2)c(e)
 -6\sum_i p_i^4.
 \label{p13:lower:exact-cumulant}
\end{align}
For example, first write
\[
 \E(1+t)^Z=\prod_i(1+p_it)
 \left[1+\sum_{2\leq|I|\leq4}
       \frac{c(I)t^{|I|}}{\prod_{i\in I}(1+p_it)}+O(t^5)\right],
\]
then take $24$ times the coefficient of $t^4$ in its formal logarithm.
This is a finite coefficient calculation; no analytic logarithm of the
true generating function is required.

Canonical direct decomposition gives
$\sum_{|I|=4}c(I)=K_4+D_{22}$, where $D_{22}$ sums
$c(e)c(f)$ over unordered disjoint pairs of edges whose spaces are direct.
In $(C_2^{\mathrm s})^2/2-D_{22}$ only repeated edges, edges sharing a
vertex, and disjoint edges with a nonzero intersection remain.
The positive propagation estimate, together with the product of the
marginals, implies
\[
 \sum_{y\ne x}|c(x,y)|\ll_{C,\eta}p_xN^\eta.
\]
Repeated edges and shared vertices consequently have total absolute
weight $O(p_*A_2N^\eta)=O(N^{-5/3+2\eta})$.

Apply the pair partition of Lemma~\ref{p13:activity:pair-partition} with
a small fixed parameter $\eta$. A product involving a weak or exceptional
edge has total weight at most
$A_2(A_{\mathrm w}+A_{\mathrm s})
\ll N^{-5/3+O(\eta)}$.
For two good edges from the remaining finite family of channels, fix the
first edge and the offset pattern of the second compression. There are
$NB^{O(1)}$ choices for the first edge. A nonzero intersection imposes
an exceptional target of fixed width, giving $N^{1/2+o(1)}$ choices for
the second compressed center by the elementary exceptional-target count
in Proposition~\ref{p1:arith:fixed-branching}. The proof of that count
uses only a fixed width and applies to this compression as well.
Each product has weight at most $N^{-10/3+o(1)}$. Hence this last cost is
$N^{-11/6+o(1)}$, and
\[
 D_{22}=(C_2^{\mathrm s})^2/2+O(N^{-5/3+\varepsilon}).
\]
The remaining terms of \eqref{p13:lower:exact-cumulant} are bounded by
$O(p_*A_3+p_*^2A_2+p_*^3\mu)$.
The triple estimate in Corollary~\ref{p13:third:activity} gives
$A_3\ll N^{-41/30+\eta}$, so each is smaller than the stated error.
This proves the first identity.

For an incompatible connected quadruple the centered expansion is
\[
 c(I)=-\prod_{i\in I}p_i
       -\sum_{\substack{J\subsetneq I\\2\leq|J|\leq3}}
             c(J)\prod_{i\in I\setminus J}p_i.
\]
The independent term sums to $O(N^{-2+\eta})$ by the connected-host
count of Corollary~\ref{p13:half:connected}. The terms with $|J|=2$ are
bounded by the fixed extension deficit
of Lemma~\ref{p13:transfer:fixed-deficit}, hence by
$O(N^{-3/2+\eta})$. For $|J|=3$, connectedness requires a non-direct
extension of its total space. The uniform independent deficit
of Lemma~\ref{p13:transfer:independent-deficit} costs $N^{-1/2+\eta}$,
and its product with $A_3$ is smaller still. Thus the total absolute
activity of incompatible connected quadruples is $O(N^{-3/2+\varepsilon})$.
Compatible coefficients are nonnegative, which proves the second identity
and then \eqref{p13:lower:positive-quartic}.
\end{proof}
